metadata.title: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq rise ahead of historic Anthropic trading debut

content.text:
US stocks rose on Thursday as investors awaited Anthropic's (ANT) public trading debut, which marks a pivotal moment for the artificial intelligence boom.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) rose 0.4%, while those on the S&P 500 (^GSPC) added 1.1%. Contracts for the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) advanced 1.8% as tech stocks surged.
All eyes are on Anthropic after the Claude maker priced its initial public offering (IPO) at $83 per share and expanded its offering to 925 million shares due to strong investor demand. At that price, Anthropic is valued at over $1 trillion, less than the market cap of SpaceX (SPCX) when it went public in June, but still larger than Walmart (WMT), Micron (MU), and AMD (AMD).
The timing of Anthropic's IPO coincides with a period of upheaval for the AI trade amid anxieties over safety, the durability of the boom, and an incoming Democratic-led Congress. The market's response to Anthropic's debut could set the tone for other companies eyeing the public markets, notably OpenAI (OPAI.PVT) — which, according to CEO Sam Altman, still plans to go public.
While Anthropic's IPO will be the main course, we'll also be paying attention to several other happenings on Thursday.
President Trump is departing the APEC Summit in China, where he met with world leaders, including Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Following Trump's visit, questions around semiconductor export controls and tariffs remained largely unanswered.
At the same time, consumer bellwether Walmart (WMT) reported a narrow earnings beat before the bell and raised its 2026 outlook. Initial jobless claims and manufacturing activity data later on in the morning will provide updates on the US's economic health.
We're also watching to see if Nvidia (NVDA) stock can shake off five straight days of losses as uncertainty over the AI chipmaker's leadership overshadowed its solid earnings report on Tuesday. Shares jumped over 3% at the open.
LIVE7 updates
David Hollerith
US stocks open higher ahead of Anthropic IPO debut
US stocks opened higher Thursday as investors awaited Anthropic's historic public-market debut, with technology shares leading gains as investors appear enthusiastic about Wall Street's artificial intelligence bonanza.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average (^DJI) rose 0.4%, while those on the S&P 500 (^GSPC) added 1%. Contracts for the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC) advanced 1.6%.
Anthropic has priced its IPO at $83 per share after strong investor demand, according to its most recent IPO paperwork, setting up what could become the largest public debut on record. The enthusiasm also lifted other AI-linked stocks, with Nvidia, AMD and Micron among chip names gaining before the bell.
Investors were also digesting Walmart earnings and fresh labor-market and manufacturing data as they waited for Anthropic shares to begin trading.
Grace O'Donnell
Stalemates over semiconductors and rare earth minerals appear little changed as Trump heads home from China
Yahoo Finance's Ben Werschkul reports:
Meetings between President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping ended Thursday with little change in ongoing economic standoffs over semiconductors, rare earth minerals, and tariffs, even as both leaders made outsized displays of personal affection.
"We have a very special relationship, and I think as long as you and I are in charge of things, we will never have a problem," Trump told Xi, who began the visit in Shenzhen by hugging Trump after he landed Wednesday.
But the leaders actively sidestepped difficult topics on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders' meeting.
At one point, they ignored a question about Jensen Huang and Nvidia (NVDA) and whether the ousted CEO was "loyal to the United States." China then barred that Bloomberg correspondent from the next photo-op, according to reporters at the event.
Walmart beats Q3 earnings expectations, raises 2026 outlook again
Walmart's (WMT) third quarter earnings came in ahead of expectations, and the retail giant raised its outlook for 2026 as e-commerce sales surged.
America's biggest retailer, often considered a bellwether for the industry and a key pulse check for what the holiday season could look like, posted revenue of $188.8 billion, just above the $187.2 billion expected, according to Bloomberg consensus data. Adjusted earnings per share clocked in at $0.65, a cent higher than $0.64.
US same-store sales growth moderated to 2.9% year over year, as analysts forecast. E-commerce sales grew 17%.
CEO John Furner said the company "delivered strong results" and its core business is "gaining market share." He added that growth is coming from several parts of Walmart's business model, including "membership and agentic shopping."
Investors are gearing up for Anthropic's IPO. Here are some of the details.
Claude AI model maker Anthropic will soon be publicly traded in a watershed moment for the artificial intelligence boom. Here are some key details to know:
What is the IPO price? $83 per share
How many shares are being offered? 980 million shares of Class A common stock total. 956,351,354 are being sold by Anthropic, and 23,648,646 are being sold by certain selling stockholders.
When will Anthropic start trading? Thursday, Nov. 19, after the market opens at 9:30 a.m. ET. There isn't a set time for when the stock will begin trading, but it's unlikely to happen right at 9:30.
What do we know about Anthropic's finances? In its amended S-1 filing, Anthropic disclosed that its sales for the nine months that ended Sept. 30 eclipsed $33 billion. It brought in $2.5 billion in all of 2025 and just $41 million in 2023.
Operating losses also improved year over year to -$1.3 billion in the first nine months of 2026 from -$5.2 billion in the same period in 2025, Yahoo Finance's Dan Howley reported.
Consumers are staying strong as AI stumbles — giving retail stocks fresh appeal
Yahoo Finance's Hamza Shaban writes:
Americans' capacity to spend continues to buoy the economy despite a cost-of-living crunch. The latest measures of consumer retail spending continue a years-long story about cash-strapped households soldering through inflation — and doing so especially as other key parts of the economy look weaker.
As the AI robots stumble, the flesh-and-blood American consumer is still out there on two feet and spending, even if they are looking for deals.
This week's corporate earnings so far show that even though there are bright spots heading into the holiday shopping season, there are still signs of stress and a renewed focus on seeking value above all else.
US retail sales slowed from September but still increased slightly in October, as households pulled back on large purchases like cars and furniture while keeping up spending elsewhere ahead of the holiday shopping season.
Oil prices steady as supply surplus softens sentiment though Gulf war supports
Reuters reports:
Oil prices were steady on Thursday after falling previously as increasing expectations for a supply surplus and higher interest rates softened sentiment, outweighing support from attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz amid the lingering Iran war.
Brent fell 1.3% in the previous session while WTI dropped 3.2% to its lowest since August 26 on emerging expectations of a supply surplus as crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have returned to roughly pre-war levels.
Prices have also come under pressure from expectations of higher US interest rates that would cause lower economic growth and slower demand increases for oil. That would also strengthen the dollar, raising prices for non-US buyers paying for dollar-denominated crude in different currencies.
Economic data: Philadelphia Fed business outlook, November (23.2 expected, 20.9 prior); Initial jobless claims, week ended Nov. 14 (197,000 expected, 200,000 prior); Continuing claims, week ended Nov. 7 (1.697 million prior); Kansas City Fed manufacturing activity, November (11 prior)
Earnings calendar: Walmart (WMT), Alibaba Group (BABA), PDD Holdings (PDD), Intuit (INTU), Ross Stores (ROST), Williams-Sonoma (WSM), Warner Music Group (WMG), The Gap (GAP), Bath & Body Works (BBWI), Webull Corporation (BULL)
